summary: Intermittent authorization failures due to OIDC token expiry skew between IdP and private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 401/403 authorization errors when calling the Redwood Private API from their VPC. Errors started after a maintenance window on the customer's IdP.

Impact:
- User-facing API calls intermittently get 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden for a subset of requests that include freshly minted OIDC tokens.
- Affects production traffic for ~10% of requests during peak; customers report failed inference requests and retry storms.

Environment:
- Customer: FinSight Analytics (private deployment)
- Redwood Private v1.8.3 running in customer-managed VPC (prod: us-west-2)
- Identity provider: self-hosted Keycloak 20.0.1
- Identity flow: OIDC ID token validated by identity-proxy on each request

Steps to reproduce:
1) Authenticate against customer's Keycloak to obtain ID token.
2) Make requests to Redwood Private endpoint with Authorization: Bearer <id_token>.
3) Repeat token issuance quickly after Keycloak maintenance or NTP adjustments.

Observed behavior / logs:
- identity-proxy logs show repeated token validation failures: "token expired" for tokens with iat very recent and exp only 120s later.
- Keycloak logs show token issuance timestamps with clock skew up to +95 seconds relative to private node time.
- Sample identity-proxy log lines:
  - [2026-03-12T18:02:10Z] auth: validation error: token expired (exp: 2026-03-12T18:04:10Z, now: 2026-03-12T18:03:05Z)
  - [2026-03-12T18:03:07Z] auth: validation error: token not yet valid (nbf: 2026-03-12T18:03:45Z, now: 2026-03-12T18:03:07Z)

Immediate customer steps taken:
- Keycloak re-synced NTP and confirmed clock drift corrected.
- Customer temporarily set their token TTL to 10 minutes to reduce failures.
comments: Customer (Aisha, FinSight): 'We started seeing 401s right after an IdP patch. It affects a subset of users and seems intermittent. We see exp timestamps in the future when compared to our app nodes.'

Support (Maya): 'Thanks Aisha — can you confirm whether your IdP time was updated during the maintenance window? Also please provide a short sample of the failing Authorization header (token omitted) and any proxied timestamps.'
Customer (Aisha): 'Yes, we rotated time sync during the window. We've attached Keycloak logs showing token issuance times. Also confirmed two app nodes show clocks ~90s behind Keycloak.'
Support (Maya): 'We've escalated to SRE for identity-proxy token validation behavior. In the meantime, increasing token leeway or temporarily extending token TTL is a viable mitigation.'

SRE (Luis): 'Investigating: initial hypothesis is OIDC exp/nbf checks are strict with default leeway=0s. We can either accept a configurable leeway in identity-proxy or advise customer to correct NTP and issue longer TTLs.'
SRE (Luis): 'Created internal patch to add configurable "oidc_token_leeway_seconds" to private deployment config and rolled to canary. Observed reduction in 401s on canary nodes.'
Customer (Aisha): 'Can confirm errors dropped on endpoints behind the canary nodes. We'll coordinate a full rollout and keep NTP in sync.'
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-12 17:55 UTC: Customer performed IdP maintenance including time sync updates.
- 2026-03-12 17:59 UTC: Increase in 401/403 observed.
- 2026-03-12 18:10 UTC: Support triaged; SRE engaged.
- 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC: Canaried identity-proxy patch adding 120s leeway.
Findings:
- Root cause: ~60-95s clock drift between Keycloak token issuer and private deployment nodes caused tokens to be seen as not yet valid or already expired depending on which direction the skew went.
- Default OIDC validation in identity-proxy did not include an automatic leeway; tokens with tight ttl (2m) are sensitive to small clock differences.
- Customer had tokens with ttl=120s which magnified the problem.
Evidence links:
- Slack thread: #support-private-auth (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123XYZ)
- Keycloak sample logs: (provided by customer)

Mitigation considered:
- Advise customer to ensure NTP sync across IdP and app nodes (recommended long-term fix).
- Add configurable token validation leeway to identity-proxy to tolerate small skews.
- Increase default token TTL recommendations in private deployment docs when using self-hosted IdPs.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: Canaried an identity-proxy config patch enabling oidc_token_leeway_seconds=120 on a subset of nodes. Observed immediate drop in 401s on canary (from ~12% to ~1%).
Customer action: FinSight re-synced NTP across all Keycloak and app hosts and increased token TTL to 10 minutes while full rollout completed.

Permanent fix: Backport patch to private-deployment helm chart introducing 'oidc.token_leeway_seconds' config and defaulting to 30s. Scheduled full rollout:
- 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC: full rollout to prod us-west-2
- Post-rollout monitoring dashboard created and anomaly alert threshold set to 5% 401 rate for 15m window.
Documentation: Added guidance to Private deployment quickstart about NTP and token TTL recommendations; created confluence page 'Private OIDC: token-leeway and NTP guidance' and linked to customer.
Follow-ups: Create automated health check that compares IdP 'now' vs node time for >30s drift and surface as warning in Redwood Console for private deployments.
